cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Warfare & the Hoplite Phalanx
cards.back: The hoplite phalanx was the dominant Greek fighting formation: a dense line of heavily armed infantry fighting shoulder to shoulder

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Warfare & the Hoplite Phalanx
cards.back: Each hoplite carried an aspis (large round shield), dory (long spear), Corinthian helmet, bronze cuirass and greaves

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Warfare & the Hoplite Phalanx
cards.back: The phalanx's strength lay in solidarity: each man's shield protected his neighbour's right side, creating an interdependent wall

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Warfare & the Hoplite Phalanx
cards.back: Naval warfare became crucial after the Persian Wars; the trireme (three-banked oared warship) was the standard warship

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Warfare & the Hoplite Phalanx
cards.back: Athens built a large navy funded by silver mines at Laurium; the thetes (poorest citizens) served as rowers, increasing their political importance

cards.front: Recall a key point about Greek Warfare & the Hoplite Phalanx
cards.back: Warfare was seasonal (summer campaigning), and war was a normal state of affairs between Greek poleis
